newsitem.title: USA: Ill. agency gets Gov's support for bond bill.
newsitem.headline: Ill. agency gets Gov's support for bond bill.

text.p: Illinois Gov. Jim Edgar will support a bill to increase by $2.9 billion the bonding authorization of Illinois Development Finance Authority, an authority official said Wednesday.

Bobby Wilkerson, the agency's director, said after meeting with Edgar's representatives earlier this month, the Edgar Administration has decided to support a bill introduced in the Illinois Senate earlier this month.

Wilkerson said the bill would increase the agency's bonding capacity in three areas -- $900 million for environmental projects, $1.5 billion for general projects including industrial revenue bonds and debt sold for 501(c)3 organizations and $500 million for local government borrowing.
He said the bill's chances were good given last week's agreement between the governor and legislative leaders on a $659 million general obligation bond authorization bill for the state.
Wilkerson said that his agency's previous requests for greater bonding capacity "got caught up" with opposition to the state bonding bill.
The authority's bonding power was last increased by the General Assembly in 1993.
